item.title: IDF chief says Israel is 'in a state of war' in Lebanon, not a ceasefire
item.description: Rockets fired from Lebanon struck northern Israel on Friday, causing power outages across the towns of Kiryat Shmona and Metula, according to Israeli Channel 12. The barrage damaged a building in Metula and sparked a fire at the scene, though no casualties were reported. The strike was part of an intensifying pattern of Hezbollah rocket fire that has made daily life in Israel's northern border communities increasingly untenable.

item.title: Zelenskyy confirms Ukraine shot down Iranian drones in Middle East
item.description:
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy publicly confirmed for the first time that Ukrainian military personnel actively shot down Iranian-designed Shahed drones in multiple Middle Eastern countries, marking a dramatic expansion of Kyiv's role in the broader conflict with Tehran. Zelenskyy made the remarks to reporters on Wednesday in a briefing embargoed until Friday, according to the Associated Press.

"Did we destroy Iranian Shaheds? Yes, we did. Did we do it in just one country? No, in several," Zelenskyy said, as reported by Euronews. He described the operations not as training exercises but as "support in building a modern air defence system that can actually work."

item.title: EU and US near critical minerals deal to counter China
item.description: The European Union and the United States are closing in on an agreement to coordinate on producing and securing critical minerals, according to a draft action plan seen by Bloomberg on Thursday. The deal is part of a broader trilateral push with Japan to break dependence on Chinese supplies of materials essential to defense, clean energy and advanced technology.

item.title: Ocean temperatures hit near-record highs in March, signaling El Niño shift
item.description: Global sea surface temperatures reached their second-highest levels on record for March, the European Union's Copernicus Climate Change Service reported on Friday, pointing to a likely transition toward El Niño conditions that could push global temperatures to new highs later this year.

item.title: Vance departs for Iran peace talks as Lebanon crisis threatens ceasefire
item.description: Vice President JD Vance departed Friday aboard Air Force Two for Islamabad, Pakistan, where he will lead what officials describe as one of the most direct US-Iran engagements since the 1979 Islamic Revolution. The first round of talks is scheduled for Saturday morning local time, with a fragile two-week ceasefire already showing signs of fracture.

item.title: Hezbollah vows to fight 'until last breath' ahead of Israel-Lebanon talks
item.description: Hezbollah Secretary-General Naim Qassem on Friday called on Lebanese officials to stop offering "free concessions" to Israel and vowed that "the resistance will continue until our last breath," sharpening the group's rhetoric just days before Israel and Lebanon are set to hold direct negotiations in Washington.

item.title: Vance departs for historic Iran peace talks in Pakistan
item.description:
Vice President JD Vance departed Washington on Friday aboard Air Force Two, bound for Islamabad, Pakistan, where he will lead what officials describe as the highest-level direct engagement between the United States and Iran since the 1979 Islamic Revolution. The talks, set to begin Saturday morning local time, come as a two-week ceasefire between the two nations teeters on the brink of collapse over Israeli military operations in Lebanon.

Boarding the plane at Joint Base Andrews, Vance struck a cautiously optimistic tone while issuing a pointed warning to Tehran. "If the Iranians are willing to negotiate in good faith, we're certainly willing to extend the open hand," he said, citing President Donald Trump. "If they're gonna try and play us, then they're gonna find that the negotiating team is not that receptive."

item.title: Ukraine nearing peace deal with Russia, top aide says
item.description:
Kyrylo Budanov, the head of Ukraine's presidential office and a key figure in peace negotiations, said he sees progress toward a potential deal with Russia to end the war, telling Bloomberg in an interview that he believes a resolution "will not take long."

"They all understand the war needs to end. That's why they are negotiating," Budanov said in an April 4 interview published on Friday. "I don't think it will be long."

item.title: UK and France deepen defense ties amid rift with Trump
item.description: The United Kingdom and France have accelerated their defense partnership in recent weeks, signing agreements on joint missile development and expanding military cooperation under the Lancaster House 2.0 framework, as both nations navigate growing tensions with the Trump administration over NATO burden-sharing and the conduct of the Iran war.

item.title: Iran sets preconditions that throw Islamabad talks into doubt
item.description: Iran's Parliament Speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf declared on Friday that two preconditions must be met before Tehran will enter negotiations with the United States in Islamabad: a ceasefire in Lebanon and the release of Iran's blocked assets abroad. The announcement, made in a post on X, has cast a shadow over talks that were scheduled to begin on Saturday under Pakistani mediation.

item.title: NASA's Artemis II crew set to splash down tonight after moon voyage
item.description: The four astronauts of NASA's Artemis II mission are hours away from returning to Earth on Friday evening, capping a 10-day journey that has produced some of the most striking space photography since the Apollo era. NASA is targeting splashdown at 8:07 p.m. EDT off the coast of San Diego, where recovery teams aboard the USS John P. Murtha will extract the crew from the Orion spacecraft, which the astronauts have dubbed Integrity.

item.title: Ocean heat waves fueling 60% more billion-dollar hurricanes, study finds
item.description:
Marine heat waves are "supercharging" the destruction caused by hurricanes and tropical cyclones around the world, according to a study published Friday in the journal Science Advances.

Researchers examined 1,600 tropical cyclones that made landfall since 1981 and found that storms passing over exceptionally warm water were more likely to undergo rapid intensification — resulting in 60% more disasters that inflicted at least $1 billion in damage, adjusted for inflation, when they reached shore.

item.title: Trump warns Iranians 'only alive to negotiate' as Hormuz remains closed
item.description:
President Donald Trump escalated his rhetoric against Iran on Friday, warning that Tehran's leadership is "only alive to negotiate" as a fragile ceasefire teetered and talks to end a six-week war neared.

"The Iranians don't seem to realize they have no cards, other than a short-term extortion of the world by using international waterways. The only reason they are alive today is to negotiate!" Trump wrote on Truth Social. He also told the New York Post that American warships were "being loaded with the best ammunition in case talks in Pakistan failed".

item.title: UK to host new allied talks on reopening Strait of Hormuz
item.description: Britain will host a new round of diplomatic talks next week with allies on reopening the Strait of Hormuz without paying tolls to Iran, according to a British official with knowledge of the planned discussions. The meeting will bring together officials from nations that participated in the 41-country summit convened by UK Foreign Secretary Yvette Cooper on April 2, making it the first such multilateral gathering since President Trump declared a two-week ceasefire with Iran on April 8.

item.title: Pope Leo XIV says 'God does not bless any conflict' amid Iran war rift with Trump
item.description:
Pope Leo XIV on Friday declared that "God does not bless any conflict," sharply escalating an extraordinary dispute between the first American pope and the American president over the use of religious language to justify the U.S. war against Iran.

"Anyone who is a disciple of Christ, the Prince of Peace, is never on the side of those who once wielded swords and now unleash bombs," the 70-year-old pontiff wrote on X, in remarks widely interpreted as aimed at President Trump and Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth, both of whom have repeatedly framed the six-week-old conflict in religious terms.

item.title: Trump's Board of Peace receives fraction of $17B pledged for Gaza
item.description: Donald Trump's Board of Peace has received less than $1 billion of the $17 billion pledged for the reconstruction of Gaza, according to sources with direct knowledge of the board's operations, leaving the U.S. president unable to advance his plans for the war-torn Palestinian territory.

item.title: Jassy defends Amazon's $200B AI bet: 'Not on a hunch'
item.description: Amazon CEO Andy Jassy used his annual shareholder letter, published Thursday, to mount a forceful defense of the company's plan to spend roughly $200 billion on capital expenditures in 2026 — the largest such corporate outlay in history — even as the tech giant continues to shed thousands of jobs.

item.title: Macron invites Trump to Versailles dinner after G7 summit
item.description:
French President Emmanuel Macron has invited U.S. President Donald Trump to a dinner at the Palace of Versailles following the Group of Seven summit in mid-June, though it remains uncertain whether Trump will attend either event, according to a Reuters exclusive report published on Thursday.

No other G7 leaders have been invited to the Versailles dinner, which is being framed as a bilateral gesture to underscore Franco-American ties ahead of the United States' 250th anniversary celebrations on July 4.

item.title: Israel, Lebanon hold first direct call ahead of Tuesday talks in Washington
item.description:
Israeli and Lebanese diplomats held a preparatory phone call on Friday ahead of the first direct negotiations between the two countries, scheduled for Tuesday, April 14, at the U.S. State Department in Washington, according to multiple officials familiar with the plans.

The call included Israeli Ambassador to the United States Yechiel Leiter, Lebanese Ambassador Nada Hamadeh Moawad, U.S. Ambassador to Lebanon Michel Issa, and State Department Counselor Mike Needham, The Wall Street Journal reported. The conversation aimed to finalize logistics for the in-person meeting, a U.S. official confirmed to The Times of Israel.

item.title: Iran admits it can't find all mines in Strait of Hormuz
item.description:
Iran has admitted it cannot locate or remove all of the naval mines it planted in the Strait of Hormuz during its war with the United States, U.S. officials confirmed on Friday, adding a dangerous new obstacle to an already fragile ceasefire and high-stakes peace negotiations set to begin in Islamabad this weekend.

The revelation, first reported by the New York Times, undercuts a central condition of the two-week ceasefire brokered earlier this week: the "complete, immediate, and safe" reopening of the world's most critical oil chokepoint. U.S. intelligence indicates that the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps used hundreds of small boats to mine the strait in a "haphazard" manner after the war began in late February, with many mine locations left unrecorded. Many of the devices have since drifted, rendering Tehran's published "safe route" charts unreliable.
